200.description: The order after release (or unchanged, if already released).

id.description: The order's identity — this bounded context's contribution to the platform.

status.description: The order-level status, ALWAYS derived from the line statuses and never stored, so it cannot drift out of sync with the lines it summarises. `Received` -> `Allocated` | `PartiallyAllocated` | `Backordered` -> `Released` | `PartiallyReleased`, with `Cancelled` reachable only from a pre-release state (BR6).
status.title: OrderStatus

requiredShipBy.description: The externally-dictated deadline this order was received with, or absent when it has none (the overwhelming majority). See the same field on ReceiveOrderRequest.

releaseOnAllocation.description: False means the order was HELD at intake (ADR 0020): allocated but deliberately not released, awaiting `POST /orders/{id}/release`. True for every order received without the flag, including every order predating ADR 0020.

promiseDate.description: The date this order is promised for, RFC 3339 — the cutoff of a CPT window computed at allocation time as a capability promise (ADR 0014): the earliest window in the site's CPT schedule that the allocated lines' process-path cycle time (P95), eligibility and wes-work-planning's path capacity can all meet. When those inputs are not available (caches cold, or no process-path catalogue configured) it falls back to the lead-time policy: "now plus the slowest configurable static lead time among the allocated lines' process paths", not a live carrier rate. With `allowPartialShipment=true` lines are promised per shipment group (ADR 0017) and this is the latest cutoff across the groups. For an order received with `requiredShipBy` it is the latest window at or before that deadline, and absent when the deadline cannot be met (ADR 0020). The promise basis (Capability / LeadTime / Network) is carried on the `OrderAllocated`/`OrderPartiallyAllocated` events, not on this response. Absent until at least one line is allocated.

capacityConstraint.description: Present on an Order ONLY when its promise overlaps a PUBLISHED warehouse-planning shortage window at the configured site (ADR 0031). The order's work window is `[now, promise cutoff)`; a window overlaps it when both half-open intervals share at least one instant (a window starting exactly at the cutoff does not). It is a derived, read-time annotation: the order is still accepted, allocated and released, its `promiseDate` is NOT moved, and nothing is reserved or revoked. Omitted entirely otherwise, so with no planning events consumed the Order response is unchanged.

constrained.description: Always true when the object is present.

site.description: The planning `location` the order was matched against — the single configured site (`PLANNED_CAPACITY_SITE_ID`, defaulting to `DEFAULT_SITE_ID`); orders do not carry a site of their own.

windows.description: The overlapping shortage windows, ordered by start.

shortage.description: Orders the planned capacity cannot process in the window.

bottleneckStep.description: The path step limiting flow, as warehouse-planning reports it.

capacityConstraint.title: CapacityConstraint

lineNo.description: The line's 1-based position within its order.

quantity.description: Quantity ordered, as received (and validated) at intake — see the matching int64 note on ReceiveOrderLineRequest.quantity.

pathId.description: The process path assigned to this line. It is chosen by this service, never by the caller (ADR 0021): the active paths in the process-path catalogue are filtered by their declared eligibility (max units, required/excluded product attributes, gift wrap) and the one with the shortest known cycle time (P95) wins, ties broken on the lower path id. With no catalogue configured, or no active path, it falls back to the default `pick`. A caller placing an order has no business supplying wes-work-planning's process-path vocabulary at intake, so this is read-only: visible in every response, never settable on the request.

status.description: The per-line status. `Pending` -> `Allocated` (inventory-storage reserved) or `Backordered` (inventory-storage answered 409); `Backordered` -> `Allocated` ONLY via retry-allocation; `Allocated` -> `Released` (a pure domain transition made in the same call once ship-complete rule BR3 allows it, ADR 0005 — the released lines are then announced on Kafka for wes-work-planning to react to independently; nothing waits for it to accept the work); any pre-release state -> `Cancelled`.
status.title: OrderLineStatus

reservationId.description: inventory-storage's reservation id, present only once the line is allocated. A reference only — this context models no local Reservation aggregate, because inventory-storage remains the sole owner of reservation state. Omitted (rather than empty) when the line is not allocated.

503.description: inventory-storage could not be reached (transport error, timeout, open circuit breaker), answered with an unexpected status, or is wired in permissive (no-op) mode. Problem `type` is `downstream-unavailable` for an infrastructure failure and `downstream-not-configured` for permissive mode. Never papered over with a 2xx: allocating real stock must not appear to succeed when it did not.
